newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Tyumen Oil Co urges unit to cooperate.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Tyumen Oil Co urges unit to cooperate.

text.p: Russia's state-owned Tyumen Oil Company, or TNK, one of the last oil giants to be privatised, urged one of its subsidiaries on Thursday to cooperate with a sale of a 40 percent TNK stake.
Tyumenskaya Neftyanyaya Kompaniya also said it was considering ways to shift most of a nearly 49 percent stake, due to be sold in a separate auction, to regional authorities.

"We have a tough line -- the investment tender must be held," Nikolai Rusanov, TNK board chairman, told a news conference, referring to a sale of 40 percent of TNK's charter capital which ends July 16.

TNK is in a major row with its subsidiary and main oil production unit Nizhnevartovskneftegaz over who should win the sale, one of the last big auctions of a Russian vertically-integrated oil company.

Rusanov said Russia's Alfa-Group, which includes commodities powerhouse Alfa-Ekho, and Rosneftinvest, an unknown entity allied with Nizhnevartovskneftegaz, were both interested in acquiring the stake. Banks and foreigners are not allowed to bid.
Rusanov said Rosinvestneft had wanted to acquire the stake outright but the government turned down the proposal.

TNK President Alexander Furman told the same news conference TNK was in talks with Tyumen regional authorities over how they could acquire most of a 48.68 TNK percent due to be sold at a special cash auction starting August 5.
AO Nizhnevartovskneftegaz produced 21.30 million tonnes of crude oil in 1996, down six percent from 1995 levels.
Russia has started bankruptcy proceedings against the producer, which owed the budget 1.10 trillion roubles ($190 million) as of June.

The 40 percent stake comprises 632.66 million shares with a fixed price of 145 billion roubles ($25 million). In addition, bidders must promise to invest at least $160 million over two years in TNK. The tender and the forthcoming special cash auction are designed to inject money into the holding company.
"For us, it's clear that without finances, we cannot develop further or find serious partners and investors," Rusanov said.

"It's important the winner have resources of $6 or $7 billion to reconstruct Samotlor and tap new reserves," he said, referring to Russia's biggest but largely idled oil field, for which TNK holds a development licence.
